findings.title: Session JSONL files are memory-mapped, so truncating one mid-scan raises SIGBUS
findings.snippet: guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url, options: [.mappedIfSafe]) else { continue }
findings.sink: Mapped Data read byte by byte in scan(data:), via firstIndex(of:) and range(of:) at ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:203-211; the same pattern is at CodexSessionScanner.swift:128 and 322-329
findings.description: On a local volume, .mappedIfSafe mmaps the file. If the file shrinks after mapping, touching a page past the new end of file raises SIGBUS, which Swift cannot catch. No snapshot, file lock or read-copy guard covers the mapped bytes while the line scanner walks them.
findings.exploit_scenario: A same-user process creates a large *.jsonl with a recent mtime in ~/.claude/projects/x/ and truncates and rewrites it in a tight loop. When a refresh maps the file and the scanner touches a page past the truncated end, the process dies with SIGBUS. Refreshes run every 300 s and on every launch, so the crash repeats.
preconditions: Winning a race between the mmap and the scan, which is easy to repeat because every refresh re-maps changed files
findings.impact: Repeatable crash of the menu-bar app (denial of service). Nothing is disclosed.
findings.fix: Read with a regular read (no .mappedIfSafe, or .uncached), or read from an open FileHandle into an owned buffer so a concurrent truncation can only produce a short read.
findings.evidence: ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:91 and CodexSessionScanner.swift:128 both use [.mappedIfSafe]; the scan loops then iterate the whole mapped Data.
